about.title: It watches. It nudges. You decide.
about.description: Many focus apps block sites or trap you in a timer. LazyNevis would rather trust you.
about.p1: During a session, LazyNevis checks the active window every second and marks the time as <focused>focused</focused>, <distracted>distracted</distracted> or <idle>idle</idle>, following the rules you set.
about.p2: If distraction goes past your limit, you get an alert: a notification, full screen or sound. What to do next is up to you. <bold>Nothing is blocked.</bold>
about.p3: It stays quietly in the tray, with global shortcuts to control the session without switching windows.

localFirst.title: Local-first
localFirst.description: All session data, settings, and audio files live in your OS application-data directory. No cloud sync.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.description: No accounts, analytics, or telemetry. The only outbound request is a manual "Check for updates" from GitHub.

noTelemetry.title: No telemetry
noTelemetry.description: Accessibility permission on your OS reads window titles only — never keystrokes. Your focus patterns stay on your machine.

about.nameText: It is "Lazy Never" run through a playful Brazilian-Portuguese accent (Mussum style): the lazy one who never gives up on focusing. Hence the motto: for the lazy, but never giving up.

features.title: Everything to make your day count
features.description: Focus, routine and habits in one app. Every feature works offline and asks nothing in return.

session.title: Focus sessions
session.description: Start, pause, resume and stop. If the app closes unexpectedly, the session comes back paused with no lost time.

classification.title: You define focus
classification.description: Choose which apps and tabs count as focus or distraction. LazyNevis simply follows your rules.

alerts.title: Alerts your way
alerts.description: A notification, full screen or sound when distraction passes the limit you set. Nothing is blocked.

breaks.title: Smart breaks
breaks.description: Get a break reminder after a stretch of focus, with a countdown.

checklist.title: Daily checklist
checklist.description: Plan with tags and due dates, and link a task to a focus session in one click.

history.title: History and export
history.description: See how your sessions went in charts and timelines. Export to JSON or CSV whenever you like.

modes.title: Compact mode and tray
modes.description: Control everything from a tiny window or the tray icon without leaving what you are doing.

customization.title: Make it yours
customization.description: English and Portuguese, light or dark theme, global shortcuts and launch at login.

privacy.title: Real privacy
privacy.description: No account, no cloud, no analytics and no telemetry. Your data stays on your computer.

pomodoro.title: Pomodoro
pomodoro.description: Focus, short-break and long-break cycles with a daily goal. Pause, skip or stop any time — and if you close the app, it picks up where you left off.

habits.title: Habits
habits.description: Set goals to check off, count, or track by volume, weight, distance or time. Log in a tap, follow your streak and get reminders.

reminders.title: Reminders
reminders.description: Remind once, daily, at an interval or monthly. Snooze, complete or dismiss, with Markdown notes and an activity log.

calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.description: See your month or week with sessions, Pomodoros, habits, checklist and reminders together. Filter and search to find anything.

howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.description: From starting a session to reviewing history, everything is transparent and under your control.

1.title: Start a session
1.description: Begin from the Dashboard or with a global shortcut whenever you are ready to focus.

2.title: Monitor active window
2.description: The monitor polls the active window every second using native OS APIs on macOS, Windows, and Linux.

3.title: Classify each second
3.description: The rule engine marks time as focused, distracted, or idle based on your allowlist or blocklist rules.

4.title: Timers accumulate
4.description: Focus, distraction, and idle totals update in real time on the Dashboard.

5.title: Alerts when needed
5.description: When distraction crosses your threshold, notifications, overlay, or sound fire — nothing is blocked.

6.title: Review history
6.description: Everything saves to local SQLite. Review timelines, charts, and exports on the History page.

install.title: Download & install
install.description: Three quick steps. No account and no app store. Pick your system and grab the installer.
install.detectedHint: We picked your system — switch the tab if that is wrong.

requirements.macos: Needs macOS 12+ on Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3…). Intel Macs are not supported yet.
requirements.linux: Needs Linux x64 (amd64). ARM64 is not supported yet.

channel.label: Which version?
channel.prereleaseHint: Newer features, less polished. Builds may be unsigned — your system might ask for a one-time allow.

install.downloadStarted: Download started — check your Downloads folder.
install.advancedCopy: I prefer to copy the command
install.prereleaseNote: Pre-releases are skipped unless you add the prerelease flag explicitly.
install.releasesError: Could not load release info. You can still download the installer or visit GitHub Releases.
install.noReleases: No installable releases are available yet. Check GitHub Releases for updates.
install.linuxHelperNote: The Linux installer detects your distro (Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Arch, and others), installs the required libraries (asks for your password), then downloads LazyNevis.
install.linuxDeps: Install these system libraries once, then continue:
install.linuxDepsCmd: sudo apt-get install libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0 libgtk-3-0 libayatana-appindicator3-1

macos.1: Click Download installer. A file named LazyNevis-install.command appears in Downloads.
macos.2: Double-click that file. A Terminal window opens and finishes the install for you.
macos.2Blocked: If macOS says it can’t be opened: right-click the file → Open → Open again.
macos.3: If Gatekeeper still blocks the app later, follow the allow guide (one-time).

windows.1: Click Download installer. A file named LazyNevis-install.cmd appears in Downloads.
windows.2: Double-click that file. A black window opens — that is normal. Wait until it says Done.
windows.2Blocked: If SmartScreen appears: More info → Run anyway.
windows.3: If Windows still blocks the app later, follow the allow guide (one-time).
windows.4: Open LazyNevis from the Start menu.

linux.1: Click Download installer. A file named LazyNevis-install.sh appears in Downloads.
linux.2: Open a terminal in that folder and run: bash LazyNevis-install.sh — or double-click if your file manager allows it. Enter your password when asked (for libraries).
linux.2Blocked: If a library install fails, open the Linux libraries guide for your distro.
linux.3: Need more help with libraries? Open the Linux libraries guide.
linux.4: Launch LazyNevis from your app menu or the path the installer printed.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.description: Quick answers about privacy, platforms and how LazyNevis works.

block.q: Does LazyNevis block sites or apps?
block.a: No. It observes, nudges and leaves the decision to you. It never blocks anything.

cloud.q: Does my data go to the cloud?
cloud.a: No. Sessions, habits, reminders, settings and audio stay in your system data folder. There is no account, cloud, analytics or telemetry.

classification.q: How does it know I am focused?
classification.a: During a session it checks the active window every second and compares it with your rules (allowlist or blocklist). It can also consider the browser tab title.

planner.q: What are Pomodoro, Habits, Reminders and Calendar?
planner.a: They are the app's routine tools. Pomodoro handles focus and break cycles; Habits tracks goals and streaks; Reminders nudges you at the right time; and Calendar brings it all into a month or week view. Everything works offline.

platforms.a: macOS 12+ (Apple Silicon), Windows 10 or 11 (x64 and ARM64) and Linux x64 (AppImage, DEB and RPM). Always download from the official GitHub Releases.

account.a: No. Download, install and use it. No login, email or sign-up.

telemetry.a: No. The only connection is the "Check for updates" button, which only reads public GitHub info when you click it.

macosPerms.q: What permissions does macOS ask for?
macosPerms.a: Accessibility (required) to read the active app and window title, never what you type. Notifications are optional and only for native alerts.

crash.q: What if the app closes mid-session?
crash.a: The session is saved every five seconds. When you reopen it, it comes back paused and you do not lose recorded time.

license.a: MIT. You can use, modify and distribute it under the license terms.

signed.a: Test builds (RC) may not be signed yet. The Gatekeeper (macOS) and SmartScreen (Windows) guides show how to allow the app once.
